purpose: Multi-arm causal estimation dataset for Week 3 budget-constrained discount optimisation in EconoCausal.

loyalty_score.note: Right-skewed toward lower values; VIP segment boosted +20 pts. High loyalty → lower price-sensitivity (already converts).

previous_purchases.note: Proxy for brand loyalty; influences both targeting and conversion.

customer_segment.note: Governs baseline conversion, price elasticity, and product tier.

campaign_channel.note: Email and push channels deliver coupons at higher rates.

product_price.note: Reflects the typical basket value for each customer archetype. Determines absolute dollar impact of discounts.

gross_margin_rate.note: Budget-seekers buy commodity items (thin margins); VIPs buy premium goods (thick margins).

customer_timestamp.note: Campaign quarter identifier for drift-detection baseline creation.

treatment_assignment.mechanism: Multinomial-logistic propensity with segment bias + Gumbel noise
treatment_assignment.description: Each customer's probability of receiving each discount tier is determined by their customer_segment (marketing selection bias) and idiosyncratic noise. Overlap is guaranteed: no tier has zero probability for any segment.
treatment_assignment.positivity_note: After softmax with noise scale=1.0, every tier receives at least ~8% probability across all segments.

outcome_generation.model: Logistic (Bernoulli) with segment-specific intercepts and HTEs

price_sensitivity_modifier.note: Younger, less-loyal customers receive up to +0.30 additional logit lift from discounts, capturing individual-level HTE heterogeneity.

outcome_generation.heterogeneity_note: Treatment effects are non-linear and segment-heterogeneous. The marginal lift of moving from $10 to $20 is smaller than moving from $0 to $10 for every segment (diminishing returns in conversion probability). Combined with thin margins, a $20 discount may generate LESS net profit than $10 for budget_seeker and casual_shopper segments.

economics.description: Discount cost is incurred ONLY when (a) the customer receives an offer AND (b) the customer purchases. A customer who receives a coupon but does not purchase incurs zero discount cost.
